members.statement_original:
Towards a complete resolution,
one of our main contributions is to quantify the empirical convergence rate of the $(2,2)$-GW distance between Euclidean mm spaces $(\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}},\|\mspace{-1mu}\cdot\mspace{-1mu}\|,\mu)$ and $(\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}},\|\mspace{-1mu}\cdot\mspace{-1mu}\|,\nu)$ of different dimensions. Abbreviating $\Delta^{\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}},\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}}}_{2}=\Delta$, the distance of interest is

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{D}(\mu,\nu) & \coloneqq\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\|\Delta\|_{L^{2}(\pi\otimes\pi)} \\ =\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}}}\big|\|x-x^{\prime}\|^{2}-\|y-y^{\prime}\|^{2}\big|^{2}d\pi\otimes\pi(x,y,x^{\prime},y^{\prime})\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
(7)

We drop subscripts from our notation because we focus on the $(2,2)$-GW case from here on out. For finiteness we will always assume $\mu\in\mathcal{P}_{4}(\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}})$ and $\nu\in\mathcal{P}_{4}(\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}})$.

members.statement_original:
Next, by expanding the $(2,2)$-GW cost, we split the EGW functional into two terms as

\[
\mathsf{S}_{\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu)=\mathsf{S}^{1}(\mu,\nu)+\mathsf{S}^{2}_{\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu),
\]
(8)

where

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{S}^{1}\mspace{-1mu}(\mu,\nu)\mspace{-3mu}\coloneqq\mspace{-3mu}\int\mspace{-3mu}\|x\mspace{-3mu}-\mspace{-3mu}x^{\prime}\|^{4}d\mu\otimes\mu(x,x^{\prime})\mspace{-3mu}+\mspace{-3mu}\int\mspace{-3mu}\|y\mspace{-3mu}-\mspace{-3mu}y^{\prime}\|^{4}d\nu\otimes\nu(y,y^{\prime})\mspace{-3mu}-4\mspace{-5mu}\int\mspace{-3mu}\|x\|^{2}\|y\|^{2}d\mu\otimes\nu(x,y) \\ \mathsf{S}^{2}_{\varepsilon}\mspace{-1mu}(\mu,\nu)\mspace{-3mu}\coloneqq\mspace{-3mu}\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\mspace{-3mu}\int\mspace{-3mu}-4\|x\|^{2}\|y\|^{2}d\pi(x,y)\mspace{-3mu}-\mspace{-3mu}8\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i\leq d_{1}\\
1\leq j\leq d_{2}\end{subarray}}\mspace{-5mu}\Big(\mspace{-3mu}\int\mspace{-3mu}x_{i}y_{j}d\pi(x,y)\Big)^{2}\mspace{-3mu}+\varepsilon\mathsf{D}_{\mathsf{KL}}(\pi\|\mu\otimes\nu).
\end{aligned}
\]
members.variant_note: The preceding main-text paragraph assumes centered measures; the decomposition is used under that standing convention.

members.statement_original:
EOT is a convexification of the classical OT problem by means of an entropic penalty. For a regularization parameter $\varepsilon>0$, EOT is given by

\[
\mathsf{OT}_{c,\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu)\coloneqq\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int c\,d\pi+\varepsilon\mathsf{D}_{\mathsf{KL}}(\pi\|\mu\otimes\nu),
\]
(4)

members.statement_original: A probability distribution $\rho\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ is called $\beta$-sub-Weibull with parameter $\sigma^{2}$ for $\sigma\geq 0$ if $\int\exp\left(\|x\|^{\beta}/2\sigma^{2}\right)d\rho(x)\leq 2$.
